the TORC2-dependent signaling network controls the activity of effector kinases, Ypk1 and Pkc1, that regulate diverse processes required for growth of yeast, and that TORC2 is a key regulator of the eisosome.
TORC2 regulates cell wall integrity and lipid homeostasis through the phosphorylation-dependent activation of Ypk1 and Pkc1.
the TORC2-dependent signaling network in S. cerevisiae controls cell wall synthesis and cell wall integrity by modulating the activity of the effector kinases Ypk1 and Pkc1.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding how TORC2 senses and responds to plasma membrane and cell wall signals to regulate the activities of Ypk1 and Pkc1, and the consequences of this regulation for the maintenance of plasma membrane and cell integrity.

understanding how TORC2, Ypk1, Pkc1, and their substrates function in a coordinated signaling network to regulate cell wall and membrane biogenesis in response to environmental and developmental cues in S. cerevisiae.
how the TORC2 signaling network regulates plasma membrane and cell wall processes, and how it integrates with the Pkh1-activated signaling pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ypk1 and Pkc1 act downstream of TORC2, to control plasma membrane and cell wall homeostasis, respectively.
TORC2, Pkh1, and Pkc1 are central regulators of cell growth, survival and adaptation to environmental stresses, and cell wall integrity.
the TORC2-dependent signaling network in S. cerevisiae is complex and highly regulated, and that it is essential for cell survival.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ypk1 and Pkc1 are key effectors of TORC2 signaling in yeast.
the TORC2-dependent signaling network in S. cerevisiae is a highly interconnected network that controls diverse processes, and is required for cell survival.
TORC2 is a master regulator of cell growth, and that TORC2-dependent signaling pathways are critical for maintaining the plasma membrane and cell wall integrity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TORC2-dependent signaling is required for cell growth and survival in response to various environmental stresses, and is also required for proper cell wall expansion.
TORC2-dependent signaling pathways are highly conserved between S. cerevisiae and mammals, with many of the same proteins and processes being regulated.
TORC2, through Ypk1 and Pkc1, controls many aspects of plasma membrane and cell wall function in S. cerevisiae.
